components.mechanism: Builds a granular-ball cover from the data and uses ball-level approximations instead of point-level neighborhoods.
components.input: A labeled feature table with a chosen granularity parameter.
components.output: A set of granular balls with labels and a ball-level rough approximation.
components.bottleneck: Point-level neighborhood computation is expensive and sensitive to noise.
components.assumption: The chosen granularity yields balls that are label-consistent enough for the downstream task.
components.cost: One cover construction pass; memory linear in the number of balls.
components.known_failure: Mixed-label balls can hide minority-class structure when the granularity is too coarse.
components.source: paper: GBCRS (IJAR 2025); card GBCRS-2025; p. 4, lines 118-146.

components.mechanism: Accumulates per-ball evidence into a class decision instead of averaging sample scores.
components.input: Granular balls with per-ball class evidence or membership masses.
components.output: A class decision with an evidence margin for each ball.
components.bottleneck: Averaging point scores discards disagreement inside a ball.
components.assumption: Per-ball evidence is comparable across balls of different sizes.
components.cost: One accumulation pass over balls; no extra model training.
components.known_failure: Evidence from large balls can dominate small but informative balls without normalization.
components.source: paper: EAC (local paper snapshot, 2025); card EAC-2025; p. 3, lines 42-68.
